question.text: Two identical cells each of emf <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> are connected in series across a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> resistance. An ideal voltmeter connected across <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> resistance reads <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. The internal resistance of each cell is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Let R1=10 Ω.

Using V=iR

i=310+2r

The voltmeter reading is V'=1.5 V.

Thus,
iR1=V'⇒10×310+2r=1.5
⇒20=10+2 r
⇒2r=10
⇒r=5 Ω
